rows.evidence: Q1: Sections II-III; the authors report their own leaf and canopy hyperspectral measurements at the Xiaotangshan experimental base in Beijing, with inoculated winter wheat, and derive and test new spectral indices (HI, PMI, YRI, AI) against observed disease index (Table I, Figs. 4-7).
rows.notes: The study only supports a precondition of the claimed effect. It shows that new spectral indices can classify healthy vs powdery mildew-, yellow rust- and aphid-infected wheat leaves (accuracies 86.5%, 85.2%, 91.6%, 93.5%; Table I) and canopy spectra (82.4%, 84.7%, 87.6%; Section III.C), and that YRI predicts yellow rust disease index at canopy scale (R2 = 0.86 on verification, Fig. 7). It does not map affected areas spatially (point spectrometer, no imagery; the authors note applicability to imaging data was not determined), and it reports nothing on farmers taking action or on preventing further pest or disease damage (pest control). Detection/severity estimation is upstream of the claimed control effect, so Q2 is no and Q3-Q9 are no by rule. For reference only: the authors note the analysis detected middle-stage disease and that early-stage detection remains a gap, and the regression reports R2 but no dispersion measure.

notes: Full text appears complete (abstract through references and biographies). Some numeric values (coordinates, p-values, R2 in places, DI category labels) are missing due to extraction of formulae/symbols, but the key results are legible. The study is a detection/identification study at leaf and single-point canopy scale at one experimental site; it contains no evidence on pest control or damage prevention.
